notes.title: Runtime Compatibility
notes.content:
In the last update, we were force to upgrade the Runtime Engine on which ClickRaid is written.  Behind the scenes, this is has been a long time coming, and we have been delaying as long as possible, as we have already identified that much of the initial code is written in a way which is incompatible with current runtimes.  Unfortunately, a bug in the runtime being used prevents us from making any further changes to the game.  We cannot even recompile on the old runtime with the old code!

Thus we spent extra time attempting to ensure full compatibility with the new runtime, so that we can continue updating the game.  However, when we released the latest update, we found for a small percentage of cases, game breaking compatibility issues remained.  We have rolled back to previous build, and have worked with players individually to restore them.

With this effort complete, we will now create and maintain a new App branch where we will publish future updates.  Thus, any fixes or new features will be applied only to this branch, however, we also understand that this branch still contains some runtime incompatibilities, and we hope to leverage this to work through the remaining incompatible code so that we can get to the point where we can once again push a stable version to default App branch.

Alternatively, there has also been some work begun on a Unity-based rewrite.  There are a significant number of benefits of pursuing a Unity-based rewrite, namely community driven recreation or even complete changes to mechanics and balance.  The maintenance team has worked closely with Slikey on this project, and gained support and blessing for taking it in a community-driven direction, mobile-first support, Steam/Discord/Kong integrations, etc.  As with any such project, the trade off of pursuing it would be the continued slow down of work on the current version. 

We are quite interested in hearing your opinions on the matter, please comment so we can make informed decisions!

The Easter event features eggs, a bunny cursor and an easter basket pet!

notes.title: Update 1.1.46
notes.content:
Sorry about not posting patch notes for yesterday, most was just trying to optimize code and find memory leaks causing FPS drops.

Anyhow this patch will hopefully cover all current issues.

-Adv damage calculation fix had a + instead of a * for the fire arrow mult.
-Ninja finally getting a buff(sorry needed to see how it compared to other classes wasnt trying to ignore anyone, as i said several time in chat he will be fixed). Consider this a test of a fix.

-Serverhost fix based on all the information i gathered the FPS drop might be due to just the sheer amount of packets the host has to send and calculate per second. The realtime mouse cursor movement seems to be the largest factor so im decrease its sync by about half. Once again if this doesnt fix the issue ill revert back but it will make other cursors movement slightly choppy and in the future i could fix this by handling movement like pet movement.
-General performance tweaks - I started using the same calculation that speeds up class projectiles on the heros with some success at decrease the amount of hero projectiles on the screen. Also i have removed the Blue XP objects from the monsters and am now just directly calculating the xp.
-Fixed merchant Xp not saving... Oops...
-Fixed some surfaces last night that wernt being cleared when they needed to be.

notes.title: Update 1.1.05
notes.content:
-Fixed Enchanter buff level bug
-Fixed a Sorc buff level bug
-Completely recoded the Charm system(I like it much better now, not spoiling all the changes just got check it out!)
-Changed the way max level is calculated. Have tried 3 different ways to do this the fairest bestest way possible. I think its perfect now... 

Long explanation:
Old system we simply added your levels up, added all the levels that came from other players and generated a % of your contribution vs the group and returned buffs from that %... yea ppl hated that...

Next we took your max level class and then compared each classes level to yours. If they were higher they were reduced... If they were lower you recieved the full bonus. If 2 of the same class existed the same rules apply and you would get those additional levels. Subclass worked the same way except it used your max level class/2

New system:
Works the same as the last except how the max level is calculated. The new system Takes all your levels and all of your current XP and adds it up into one pool containing all the Class XP you have ever earned. Then it runs it through the same leveling formula all the heros go through(as if you played 1 class since you started playing a class). This spits out the highest level you could have achieved and is now your Max level to compare to others with.   The problem with the 2nd system was it punished you for not playing a single class. New system lets you play anything you want without preventing you from recieving the buff levels you deserve.  This system had to be developed to prevent high levels from making the game to easy on the lower level players that were just hitting 650.
